title: Finding the Right Words: Communication in Complex Patient Care
learning_goal: Apply therapeutic communication techniques, recognize communication barriers, and select appropriate communication strategies when caring for a patient whose condition impairs verbal expression.
target_audience: Nursing students and early-career nurses learning foundational communication competencies in clinical practice.
visual_style: 2D semi-flat limited animation with clean linework and muted clinical color palette. Characters express emotion through head tilts, hand gestures, posture shifts, and facial expressions. Mouth movement suggests speech without phoneme-level lip sync. Consistent character proportions and clothing across all scenes.

appearance.hair: Black, pulled back in a low bun, with small gold stud earrings
appearance.uniform: Navy blue scrub top and pants, hospital ID badge clipped to left chest, white sneakers
appearance.distinguishing_features: Thin-framed rectangular glasses, calm and attentive expression as baseline

characters.name: Harold
characters.role: Patient, 71-year-old male, post-stroke with expressive aphasia

appearance.build: Slightly heavyset, average height, seated in hospital bed
appearance.uniform: Light blue hospital gown, thin blanket over lap
appearance.distinguishing_features: Mild right-sided facial droop, uses left hand predominantly, frustrated expression when unable to communicate

characters.emotional_baseline: Anxious, frustrated, and eager to be understood

appearance.uniform: Dark teal scrub top and pants, hospital ID badge, white clogs
appearance.distinguishing_features: Reading glasses pushed up on forehead, clipboard in hand

setting.location: Medical-surgical unit, private patient room, mid-sized hospital
setting.scene_description: A single-occupancy hospital room with a bed centered against the back wall. There is a bedside table to the right of the bed with a water pitcher, a call button, and a small whiteboard mounted on the wall beside the bed with dry-erase markers. A visitor chair sits to the left. A wall-mounted monitor displays vitals. The doorway to the corridor is on the left side of the room. The room is clean, functional, and modest in detail.

background_furniture.name: Bedside table

background_furniture.name: Visitor chair
background_furniture.description: Padded chair with wooden arms, positioned to the left of the bed

background_furniture.name: Whiteboard
background_furniture.description: Small dry-erase whiteboard mounted on the wall next to the bed, partially filled with care notes and a simple drawn pain scale

scenes.scene_summary: Nurse Maya enters Harold's room for a morning assessment. Harold had a stroke three days ago and has expressive aphasia — he understands speech but cannot reliably produce words. He becomes visibly frustrated, attempting to speak but producing only fragmented sounds. Maya must decide how to begin communicating effectively with him.
scenes.character_actions: Maya enters the room holding a small tablet and a pen. She approaches the bed, smiling gently. Harold turns his head toward her, raises his left hand in a partial wave, then opens his mouth. He produces a strained, broken syllable — not a word — and his expression shifts to frustration. He looks away and grips the bed rail.

initial_character_positions.position: Entering through the doorway on the left, walking toward the foot of the bed
Seated upright in the hospital bed, slightly turned toward the door

dialogue.line: Good morning, Mr. Harold. I'm Maya, your nurse today. I'm here to check in with you and see how you're feeling.
dialogue.character_position: Standing at the foot of the bed, making eye contact with Harold

dialogue.line: I— I— ngh... I wan— I—
dialogue.character_position: In the bed, leaning slightly forward, face tightening with effort and frustration

dialogue.line: Take your time. I'm not in a rush, and I want to understand you.
dialogue.character_position: Moving to the left side of the bed, maintaining calm eye contact

audio.sound_effects: Soft footsteps on linoleum; faint monitor beeping in the background
audio.ambience: Low ambient hospital hum, distant corridor sounds

scenes.scene_summary: Maya asks Harold a series of open-ended verbal questions, expecting him to respond in full sentences. Because Harold has expressive aphasia, this approach produces only escalating frustration. He cannot generate the verbal output being requested, and the interaction breaks down.
scenes.character_actions: Maya holds her tablet and reads questions from it, looking up at Harold expectantly after each one. Harold attempts to answer, producing fragmented sounds. His left hand moves in an agitated gesture. He turns his head away from Maya and closes his eyes. Maya pauses, visibly uncertain about how to proceed.

initial_character_positions.position: Standing at the left side of the bed, holding tablet at chest level
In the bed, head tilting forward with effort, then turning away

dialogue.line: Can you tell me what's bothering you most right now? And how would you describe your pain?
dialogue.character_position: Standing beside the bed, looking at Harold with a focused expression

dialogue.line: I— the— ngh...
dialogue.character_position: In the bed, straining with effort, then going still and turning his head away

dialogue.line: I'm sorry, I think I need to try a different approach to help us communicate better.
dialogue.character_position: Standing at the bedside, lowering the tablet slightly

audio.sound_effects: Monitor beeping continues; brief silence after Harold goes quiet

scenes.scene_summary: Maya uses closed-ended yes/no questions along with the whiteboard pain scale and simple gesture cues, adapting her communication to match Harold's actual ability to respond. Harold is able to indicate his pain level and nod or shake his head, and his posture visibly relaxes.
scenes.character_actions: Maya steps to the whiteboard, points to the simple drawn faces on the pain scale, then holds up one finger and nods, demonstrating a yes gesture. She uses calm, short questions. Harold watches attentively and uses a head nod and a left-hand thumbs-up. His facial expression eases from frustration to a more settled look. Maya nods in return and makes a note on her tablet.

initial_character_positions.position: Standing at the left side of the bed, angled slightly toward the whiteboard
In the bed, head turned toward Maya and the whiteboard

dialogue.line: Let me make this easier. I'll ask you simple questions — just nod for yes, or shake your head for no. Can you show me on this scale where your pain is?
dialogue.character_position: Standing beside the bed, pointing to the whiteboard pain scale

dialogue.line: [nods, then points left hand toward the middle of the pain scale]
dialogue.character_position: In the bed, leaning slightly forward, expression more relaxed

dialogue.line: Good, that helps me a lot. We'll work together like this, and I'll make sure everyone on your team knows what works for you.
dialogue.character_position: Standing at the bedside, noting on tablet, offering a small reassuring nod

audio.sound_effects: Soft dry-erase marker sound as Maya gestures near the board; monitor beeping continues

scenes.scene_summary: Maya, interpreting Harold's frustration as emotional distress rather than a communication barrier, calls the charge nurse to intervene with counseling. Charge nurse Deb arrives, realizes the root issue is Harold's expressive aphasia rather than an emotional crisis, and redirects the situation.
scenes.character_actions: Maya steps back from the bed and moves toward the door, speaking quietly into the hallway. Deb enters shortly after, holding her clipboard. Deb looks at Harold, then at Maya. She gestures gently toward the whiteboard. Maya's expression shows that she understands she misidentified the barrier.

initial_character_positions.position: Near the doorway, speaking toward the hallway
In the bed, watching the doorway with a tired expression
Entering through the doorway, clipboard in hand

dialogue.line: I got your message. What's going on, Maya?
dialogue.character_position: Standing just inside the doorway, glancing between Maya and Harold

dialogue.line: He seems really upset and won't respond to me. I thought he might need emotional support.
dialogue.character_position: Near the doorway, keeping her voice low

dialogue.line: His aphasia means he can't produce words — his understanding is intact. Try the whiteboard and yes/no questions. That's the communication barrier here.
dialogue.character_position: Stepping toward the bed, gesturing toward the whiteboard on the wall

audio.sound_effects: Soft footsteps as Deb enters; monitor beeping continues

scenes.scene_summary: Later in the morning, Maya is preparing to provide medication education for Harold's newly prescribed blood pressure medication. Harold's son left a note stating the family would like to be present for all teaching. Harold's son is not currently in the room. Maya must decide how to handle the teaching moment.
scenes.character_actions: Maya enters the room holding a printed medication sheet. She sees the handwritten note on the bedside table. She reads it, glances at Harold, and then looks at the medication sheet. Harold watches her, his left hand resting on his lap, his expression attentive and expectant.

initial_character_positions.position: Entering from the doorway, moving to the bedside table to review the note
In the bed, head turned toward Maya, watching

dialogue.line: Mr. Harold, I have information about your new blood pressure medication I'd like to go over with you.
dialogue.character_position: Standing at the bedside table, holding the printed medication sheet

dialogue.line: I see your son left a note asking to be here for any teaching. He's not in the room right now.
dialogue.character_position: Standing at the bedside, looking from the note to Harold

dialogue.line: [nods slowly, then points to the note and holds up one finger as if to say 'wait']
dialogue.character_position: In the bed, gesturing deliberately toward the note

audio.sound_effects: Paper rustle as Maya holds the medication sheet; soft monitor beeping
audio.ambience: Low ambient hospital hum, a distant cart rolling in the hallway

scenes.scene_summary: Maya proceeds with the full verbal medication education without waiting for Harold's son and without providing written materials. Because Harold cannot verbally confirm understanding and has no written reference, the information is not retained and the son arrives to find no teaching has been documented or reinforced.
scenes.character_actions: Maya begins reading the medication information aloud from the sheet. Harold listens but cannot ask questions or respond verbally. Maya finishes, sets the sheet face-down on the table, and turns to leave. A moment later, Harold's son steps in, looks at his father, then at the table, and asks Maya a question. Maya pauses, looking uncertain.

initial_character_positions.position: Standing at the left side of the bed, holding the medication sheet
In the bed, watching Maya, expression neutral but slightly passive

dialogue.line: I'll go ahead and walk you through it now. This medication lowers your blood pressure and should be taken once daily in the morning.
dialogue.character_position: Standing at the bedside, reading from the sheet

dialogue.line: Do you have any questions? — I know that's hard to answer right now. I'll leave this here.
dialogue.character_position: Setting the sheet face-down on the table, preparing to leave

dialogue.line: I should have waited and also given him something written to follow along. Let me come back and do this properly with you both.
dialogue.character_position: Pausing near the doorway after Harold's son enters, turning back to the room

audio.sound_effects: Paper placed on table; footsteps near the door

scenes.scene_summary: Maya decides to postpone all teaching entirely and documents that teaching was deferred, without providing Harold any introductory information or written materials in the meantime. When Deb reviews the chart later, she notes the missed teaching opportunity and follows up with Maya.
scenes.character_actions: Maya sets the medication sheet back in her folder and steps toward the door. Harold looks at her with a questioning tilt of his head. Later, Deb is seen in the hallway looking at a tablet. She flags down Maya with a calm but direct expression.

initial_character_positions.position: Near the doorway, folder in hand
In the bed, watching Maya leave with a slightly puzzled expression
In the hallway just outside the room, appearing after a scene cut

dialogue.line: I'll hold off on teaching until his son is here. I'll mark it as deferred.
dialogue.character_position: Near the doorway, speaking quietly to herself as she notes on the tablet

dialogue.line: Maya, I see teaching for Mr. Harold was fully deferred. Did you leave him anything written in the meantime?
dialogue.character_position: In the hallway, tablet in hand, tone professional and curious

dialogue.line: No, I didn't. I see now I could have given him the handout and introduced the key points, even without his son present.
dialogue.character_position: In the hallway, facing Deb, expression reflective

audio.sound_effects: Soft footsteps in the hallway; ambient corridor sounds
audio.ambience: Brighter hallway ambient sound, slightly busier than the room

scenes.scene_summary: Maya honors Harold's request to wait, provides him the printed medication sheet to review independently using visual communication, and documents the plan to complete teaching with his son present. When the son arrives shortly after, Maya conducts the teaching using multiple communication forms and confirms understanding through return demonstration with the son.
scenes.character_actions: Maya holds the medication sheet up so Harold can see it clearly, points to the key sections, and places it on his bedside table within reach. She writes a brief note on the whiteboard: 'Teaching with son — soon.' Harold nods and gives a thumbs-up with his left hand. His son arrives at the doorway. Maya turns toward him, gestures welcomingly, and the three of them engage in a brief, calm teaching session. Maya concludes by asking the son to summarize the key point back to her.

initial_character_positions.position: Standing at the left side of the bed, holding the medication sheet toward Harold
In the bed, looking at the sheet, expression attentive and settled

dialogue.line: I understand — we'll wait for your son. Here's the information sheet so you can look it over. I'll note our plan on the board.
dialogue.character_position: Standing at the bedside, placing the sheet on the table and stepping to the whiteboard

dialogue.line: [nods and gives a thumbs-up with left hand]
dialogue.character_position: In the bed, visibly more at ease, glancing at the medication sheet

dialogue.line: Great — I'll be back once he arrives and we'll go through everything together. Can you tell me back the one thing you want to make sure we cover?
dialogue.character_position: Turning toward the doorway as Harold's son appears, welcoming him into the room

audio.sound_effects: Dry-erase marker sound at whiteboard; soft footsteps as son enters
audio.ambience: Low ambient hospital hum; calm, quiet room

decision_points.question_text: Harold has expressive aphasia following his stroke — he understands what is said to him, but he cannot reliably produce words. He is showing clear signs of frustration. What is the most appropriate communication approach for Maya to use right now?

choices.text: Shift to closed-ended yes/no questions and use the whiteboard pain scale with visual cues, adapting communication to match Harold's actual ability to respond.
Continue asking open-ended verbal questions and give Harold more time to formulate his answers, since encouraging verbal attempts will help him practice speech.
choices.misconception: Confuses the communication barrier created by expressive aphasia with a need for more time. Open-ended verbal questions place demands on a patient who cannot produce language, escalating frustration rather than facilitating communication. Adjusting the form and structure of questions is the appropriate response.

choices.text: Call the charge nurse to come provide emotional support counseling, since Harold's frustration suggests he may be experiencing a psychological crisis.
choices.misconception: Misidentifies the primary barrier as emotional or psychological rather than recognizing it as a physical and linguistic communication barrier caused by the patient's neurological condition. Expressive aphasia requires adapted communication strategies, not crisis counseling.

decision_points.question_text: Harold has communicated through gesture that he would like his son present for the medication teaching. His son is not currently in the room. What should Maya do?

choices.text: Honor Harold's request, give him the printed medication sheet to review as a visual reference, note the teaching plan on the whiteboard, and return to conduct the full teaching session with his son present.
Proceed with the full verbal teaching session now since Harold is awake and alert, to ensure the information is not delayed.
choices.misconception: Overlooks the patient's expressed preference and the importance of using multiple communication forms. A patient with expressive aphasia cannot ask clarifying questions during verbal-only teaching, and proceeding without a support person or written materials reduces the effectiveness of the education and disregards the patient's wishes.

choices.text: Defer all teaching entirely and document it as postponed, to avoid giving Harold incomplete information.
choices.misconception: Fails to recognize that patient teaching should be ongoing and that providing a written reference and introducing key points is both appropriate and beneficial in the interim. Completely deferring without any educational support misses a teaching opportunity and may delay the patient's understanding of their care.
